_note: Article 5(1) AI Act, simplified. A practice is prohibited only if ALL its criteria are met and no exception applies. Not legal advice.

practices.name: Harmful manipulation or deception
criteria: uses subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness, or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques
with the objective or effect of materially distorting the behaviour of people by impairing their ability to make an informed decision
causing, or reasonably likely to cause, significant harm
examples: an app using hidden audio cues to push users into gambling far beyond their means

practices.name: Exploitation of vulnerabilities
criteria: exploits vulnerabilities of a person or group due to age, disability or a specific social or economic situation
with the objective or effect of materially distorting their behaviour
causing, or reasonably likely to cause, significant harm
examples: a toy with a voice assistant encouraging children to do dangerous challenges

practices.name: Social scoring
criteria: evaluates or classifies people over a period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal characteristics
the resulting score leads to detrimental treatment in social contexts unrelated to where the data was collected, OR to treatment that is unjustified or disproportionate to their behaviour
examples: a city scoring residents on their online behaviour and restricting access to public housing for low scores

practices.name: Predicting criminal offences based solely on profiling
criteria: assesses or predicts the risk that a person will commit a criminal offence
based solely on profiling or on assessing personality traits and characteristics
exceptions: systems that support a human assessment of a person's involvement in a crime that is already based on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity
examples: a tool predicting who will commit theft from their personality profile and neighbourhood

practices.name: Untargeted scraping of facial images
criteria: creates or expands facial recognition databases
through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage
examples: crawling social media photos to build a face search engine

practices.name: Emotion recognition at work or in education
criteria: infers the emotions of a natural person
in the workplace or in education institutions
exceptions: systems intended for medical or safety reasons (e.g. detecting a pilot's or driver's fatigue)
examples: a webcam tool scoring employees' enthusiasm during video meetings

practices.name: Biometric categorisation inferring sensitive attributes
criteria: categorises individual people based on their biometric data
to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation
exceptions: labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets, or categorisation in the area of law enforcement
examples: analysing face photos to infer sexual orientation

practices.name: Real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement
criteria: real-time remote biometric identification (e.g. live facial recognition)
in publicly accessible spaces
for the purpose of law enforcement
exceptions: strictly necessary for: the targeted search for victims of abduction, trafficking or sexual exploitation, or missing persons; preventing a specific, substantial and imminent threat to life or a genuine threat of a terrorist attack; locating or identifying suspects of serious crimes listed in Annex II. Requires prior authorisation and other safeguards (Art. 5(2)-(7)).
examples: police running live facial recognition on all cameras of a train station to find shoplifters

practices.name: Non-consensual intimate or sexually explicit depictions
criteria: generates or manipulates intimate or sexually explicit images, video or audio of an identifiable real person
without that person's consent
and this is the intended purpose, or a reasonably foreseeable outcome without adequate safeguards
practices.note: Added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. See the timeline in SOURCES.md.
examples: a 'nudify' app that undresses photos of real people

practices.name: Generation of child sexual abuse material
criteria: generates child sexual abuse material
and this is the intended purpose, or a reasonably foreseeable outcome without adequate safeguards
practices.note: Added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. See the timeline in SOURCES.md.
examples: an image generator without safeguards that reproducibly produces such material
